claims.text: Mild to moderate disease: fluconazole or itraconazole; severe: amphotericin B.
claims.quote: For mild to moderate disease, fluconazole or itraconazole For severe disease, amphotericin B

claims.text: Primary infection w risk factors for severe or progressive disease: treat;
claims.quote: Patients with primary coccidioidomycosis and risk factors for severe or progressive disease should be treated.

claims.text: most immunocompetent pts w mild initial pulmonary infection need no antifungal, but PO fluconazole for 3 to 6 mo may be considered if Sx are prolonged or severe.
claims.quote: Most immunocompetent patients with mild initial pulmonary infection do not require antifungal therapy, especially if asymptomatic, but oral fluconazole for 3 to 6 months may be considered if symptoms are prolonged or severe

claims.text: Mild to moderate nonmeningeal extrapulmonary disease: fluconazole or itraconazole; voriconazole or posaconazole are alternatives (not well studied).
claims.quote: Mild to moderate nonmeningeal extrapulmonary involvement should be treated with fluconazole or itraconazole. Voriconazole or posaconazole delayed-release tablets are alternatives but have not been well-studied.

claims.text: Severe illness: lipid amphotericin B preferred over conventional;
claims.quote: For severe illness, lipid formulations of amphotericin B are preferred over conventional amphotericin B.

claims.text: switch to an oral triazole once stable (usually within several weeks).
claims.quote: Patients can usually be switched to an oral triazole once they have been stabilized, usually within several weeks.

claims.text: Meningeal disease: fluconazole, then lifelong azole maintenance (relapses are common and potentially fatal).
claims.quote: For meningeal coccidioidomycosis, fluconazole is used. The optimal dose is unclear; a high oral dose once a day may be more effective. Patients should continue azole maintenance therapy for life because relapses are common and potentially fatal.

claims.text: Immunocompromised: maintenance PO fluconazole or itraconazole until CD4 > 250 cells/mcL on HAART.
claims.quote: Immunocompromised patients with coccidioidomycosis require maintenance therapy to prevent relapse; oral fluconazole or oral itraconazole usually is sufficient and is administered until the CD4 cell count becomes > 250 cells/mcL on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART).

claims.text: Preg: avoid triazoles in the first trimester (teratogenic);
claims.quote: In pregnant patients, triazole antifungals should be avoided in the first trimester because of the risk of teratogenicity.

claims.text: severe or extrapulmonary disease in the first trimester: amphotericin B.
claims.quote: For women with severe or extrapulmonary disease in the first trimester, treatment with amphotericin B is recommended.
